about: NC Envirothon station check-ins (ENVTEST). pre = the real 2026 Area 8 middle-school test, post = the 2022 Area 8 MS test (CEI: the 2026 form again). Every kept question is verbatim from the source, with its answer key and cite. ans = the index of the keyed choice (0 = A); a list = a 'select all that apply' item (all must be picked). Items that need a picture, a specimen, or the Rowan County Soil Survey tables are listed under dropped.

items.q: When it comes to evaluating news sources, stories, and confirming creditability, it can be tough to know who to trust. It is important to avoid baiting and click-bait tactics. Select the option the best describes “baiting”:
choices: When the news source puts a virus on the click baiter’s device and hooks them forever by getting all of their personal information, thus baiting them
Using sensationalized language such as vague, misleading, and/or exaggerated headlines to purposely drive clicks to a news source
Only focusing on one angle or side of a debate or controversy, while ignoring or distorting the other perspectives to bait one-sided viewers to particular news sites
Publishing a demonstrably false claim without correcting it to drive more clicks to a news source

items.q: Which of the following options are true when looking for credible, legitimate news sources? Select all that apply.
choices: They take accountability in their mistakes, correcting information as necessary.
They abide by ethical guidelines and standards that are made available to the public, oftentimes in the form of editorial policies or a code of ethics.
They provide information from state-run and/or state-sponsored campaigns to further national agendas.
They consistently focus on one angle of their stories to minimize confusion.
